title: Eka Robotics raises $150M to teach robots to grip by feel
content:
Eka Robotics, a Cambridge, Massachusetts startup building robots that handle objects by touch as well as sight, has raised a $150M Series A. Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and F-Prime led the round, Eka announced on its blog on Tuesday. The round values the company at $1.45B post-money, Tim Fernholz reported for TechCrunch.
F-Prime is a venture fund linked to FMR, the parent company of Fidelity Investments. Obvious Ventures and E14 Fund, which led Eka’s seed round, invested again. MFV Partners, Bison Ventures, Glasswing Ventures, Samsung Next and several unnamed large companies also took part. Eka says the money will help it train its model on more tasks and speed up customer deployments.
Touch, not only sight
Many robot AI models connect what a robot sees and the instructions it gets to the actions it takes. Eka’s model adds force. It combines vision with feedback from force sensors in the robot’s hand, so the robot can feel a grip slipping and correct it.
“Vision is not the primary way in which you close this last millimeter problem. Vision tells you roughly where the object is, what the pose is, but the actual grabbing, the actual searching is happening through forces,” co-founder Pulkit Agrawal told TechCrunch.
Eka designed its own hand for this, with more force sensors than a standard gripper, TechCrunch reported. Agrawal said the hardware costs less than $1,000. It is rated for 5 million duty cycles, and the goal is 20 million, the level of standard industrial arms.
Others are working on robot touch too. Zurich’s Enact raised $30M this week to give robots a sense of touch. In China, robot-hand maker Linkerbot was seeking a $6bn valuation in May.
Practice in simulation
Much of the robotics industry teaches machines with recordings of people doing the task. Eka trains by trial and error in a physics simulator instead, using reinforcement learning, then moves the skills onto real hardware. It says it can generate thousands of hours of robot experience in minutes.
The founders met as graduate students at the University of California, Berkeley. Agrawal leads the Improbable AI Lab at MIT. Tuomas Haarnoja worked at Google DeepMind and co-created Soft Actor-Critic, a widely used reinforcement learning algorithm.
Other startups collect human data instead. Maxinsights raised $30M this week to turn household chores into robot training data.
1,500 picks an hour
Eka says its robots pick objects they were not trained on at 1,500 an hour, about two and a half times the human rate of around 600. The same robot can screw in a light bulb and insert wires. According to TechCrunch, it handles objects of up to 1 kg and succeeds more than 95% of the time. TNW has not verified those figures.
“Eka’s Vision-Force-Action model is the first approach I’ve seen that truly solves manipulation with the generality and throughput needed for deployments,” said Raghu Raghuram of a16z in Eka’s announcement.
Kris Hauser, a professor at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, told TechCrunch the robot had a “wow factor” and adapted to many objects without retraining.
The factory test
Eka is running pilots with industrial customers in pick-and-place and wire handling, TechCrunch reported. It has not named them. Hauser said the real test comes on the production line.
“What’s going to be a big challenge is when they work with integrators on real assembly lines, and it needs to run without breaking for an entire year,” Hauser told TechCrunch.

report.summary: Eka Robotics 融资 1.5 亿美元，用“视觉+力觉”教机器人精细抓取
report.background: 长期以来，机器人操作依赖视觉：先看清物体位置，再规划动作。但抓取的最后几毫米——比如捏住滑动的螺丝、插线——视觉难以精确判断，力觉反馈才是关键。Eka Robotics 由 UC Berkeley 同学 Pulkit Agrawal（现 MIT 教授）与 Tuomas Haarnoja（Soft Actor-Critic 算法共同作者）创办，自研带多枚力传感器、成本不足 1000 美元的手爪，在物理仿真中强化学习海量试错后迁移到真机。本周 a16z 与 F-Prime 领投 1.5 亿美元 A 轮，投后估值 14.5 亿美元，跟投者包括三星 Next 等。同期瑞士 Enact、中国灵巧手厂商也在追逐触觉赛道。
key_points: Eka 的模型在“视觉—指令—动作”链条中加入力反馈，机器人能感到抓握即将滑脱并实时纠正，解决视觉够不着的最后几毫米问题。
硬件是自研手爪，力传感器多于通用夹爪，单只成本低于 1000 美元，额定 500 万次作业循环，目标提升到工业级 2000 万次。
训练不靠人类演示录像，而是在物理仿真器里用强化学习试错，几分钟可生成数千小时机器人经验，再迁移到真机。
官方称机器人每小时可抓取 1500 件未经训练过的物体，约为人工 600 件的 2.5 倍，成功率超 95%（未经第三方验证）。
已在工业客户处试点分拣与线缆处理，但学界提醒：真实产线需连续一年无故障运行，才是真正的考验。
report.impact: 对 AI 行业，这标志着机器人基础模型从“视觉—语言—动作”扩展到“视觉—力觉—动作”，触觉数据与仿真训练成为新竞争维度，14.5 亿美元估值显示资本对具身智能的押注仍在加码。对开发者，仿真强化学习加低成本力觉硬件的路线可复现性强，相关算法与硬件值得关注。对普通用户，短期内影响有限，但插线、装配等精细工种自动化的时间表可能提前，物流与制造业岗位结构将逐步变化。
report.tools: 想跟进可关注：强化学习算法 Soft Actor-Critic（Eka 联创参与创建）、MuJoCo/Isaac Sim 等物理仿真器做触觉训练；硬件侧可研究低成本力/触觉传感器与开源灵巧手项目（如 LEAP Hand、DexRobot 生态）；同赛道公司 Enact、Linkerbot 也值得跟踪。
